subject: general
question: Which British Prime Minister officially announced the decision to grant independence to India and withdraw British forces from the subcontinent?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Clement Atlee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clement Atlee**, the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1945 to 1951**, officially announced the decision to grant independence to India in **February 1947**.
 
• This decision marked a significant turning point in history, as the British Empire had ruled India for nearly **200 years**.
 
• The announcement was made in the context of mounting **Indian nationalist movements**, including the efforts of leaders such as **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Jawaharlal Nehru**, and the **INA activities** led by **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose**. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• Atlee declared the British intention to **withdraw from India** by June 1948. This decision was influenced by several factors such as the **economic strains** caused by World War II, growing pressure from **Indian independence movements**, and increasing difficulties in administering the colony.
 
• The process of independence was expedited by the appointment of **Lord Mountbatten** as the last Viceroy of India. Mountbatten worked to ensure a smooth transition, leading to the partition of India into **India and Pakistan** on **15th August 1947**. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• Atlee’s government also considered the ongoing communal violence between Hindus and Muslims, which led to the decision to partition the subcontinent. This was done to avoid further bloodshed and facilitate a manageable governance structure. Hence, statement is correct.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Clement Atlee.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Leading to India's Independence:**

 
 
• The **Second World War** (1939-1945) left Britain economically weakened, making it challenging to sustain its colonial rule in India.
 
• The rise of **Indian nationalist movements**, particularly the **Quit India Movement** of 1942, demonstrated the demand for complete independence and made colonial administration increasingly difficult.
 
• The **Royal Indian Navy Mutiny** (1946) and unrest in armed forces also showed Britain the declining control over its colonial subjects.
 
 
 
• **Role of Clement Atlee:**
 
 
• **Clement Atlee** was the first British Prime Minister to acknowledge that the colonial rule in India was no longer sustainable.
 
• He appointed **Lord Mountbatten** as Viceroy in 1947 to oversee the transition to independence and ensure that the process was completed peacefully.
 
• Atlee’s Labour government was ideologically inclined towards **decolonization**, which aligned with its domestic focus on social reforms and economic recovery.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India:**
 
 
• The communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims led to the decision to partition India into two nations – **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• The partition resulted in large-scale migration and violence, with millions displaced and thousands killed.
 
• The partition was enacted under the **Indian Independence Act, 1947**, which was passed by the British Parliament.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Contributions of Clement Atlee:**

 
 
• He played an instrumental role in ending colonial rule in India, marking the beginning of decolonization across the world.
 
• His government’s policies focused on ensuring a peaceful transition while addressing communal tensions in the subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Figures:**
 
 
• **Stafford Cripps:** Known for the **Cripps Mission** in 1942, which aimed to grant dominion status to India but failed due to lack of support.
 
• **Pethick Lawrence:** As Secretary of State for India, he emphasized negotiations and was part of the **Cabinet Mission** in 1946.
 
• **Winston Churchill:** Churchill, a staunch imperialist, opposed granting independence to India during his tenure as Prime Minister before Atlee.
